column1: # boru Language Specification: boru:fn-util — the point-free function
# vocabulary (FnUtil namespace)
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# The module ships the audit's §6.4 recommendation
# (design/HIGHER-ORDER-FUNCTIONS.0.md): compose, pipe, curry, partial,
# const, identity, flip, on, memoize. Only the rows that COMPILE live
# here (the main corpus holds refusalCeiling = 0). The behaviour rows
# def-bind a computed fn — refused as "def-bound computed fn apply (closure
# shape unknown — Stage 1)", the §5.4 / NUR101 family, until 2026-09-08
# (the thirty-fifth increment, the def-bound computed-fn model): the
# producing word claims the wrapper's arity in check mode, the check pass
# models the bound wrapper's word dispatch at the read, and the VM applies
# the wrapper on its own signatures. The curried-chain row still refuses
# and stays in lang/spec/frontier/frontier-fn-util.tsv.
import "boru:fn-util"  FnUtil.identity 42
import "boru:fn-util"  FnUtil.identity 'v'
# The REFUSAL rows compile: curry's shape checks run inside the native,
# on an operand the recorder now bakes as an inert const (the family's
# CompileStoresFn declaration), so the compiled lane raises the same
# type_error the interpreter does.
import "boru:fn-util"  def f fn [a:Integer Integer [a] s:String String [s]] end def c (FnUtil.curry f/v)
column2: ERROR:FnUtil.curry: the function must have exactly one signature, got 2 overloads

column1: import "boru:fn-util"  def f fn x:Integer Integer [x] end def c (FnUtil.curry f/v)
column2: ERROR:FnUtil.curry: the function must take at least 2 parameters, got 1

column1: # The BEHAVIOUR rows (graduated 2026-09-08, the thirty-fifth increment): a
# def-bound wrapper's read is its word dispatch, modelled at the read over
# the wrapper's arity of fixed tokens inside the statement.
import "boru:fn-util"  def addone x:Integer => [add 1 x] end def double x:Integer => [mul 2 x] end def h (FnUtil.compose addone/v double/v) end (h 5)
import "boru:fn-util"  def addone x:Integer => [add 1 x] end def double x:Integer => [mul 2 x] end def h (FnUtil.pipe addone/v double/v) end (h 5)
import "boru:fn-util"  def k (FnUtil.const 7) end (k 99)
import "boru:fn-util"  def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]] end def fs (FnUtil.flip sub2/v) end (fs 3 10)
column3: flip reverses the signature order: sub2 10 3

column1: import "boru:fn-util"  def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]] end def p (FnUtil.partial sub2/v 10) end (p 3)
import "boru:fn-util"  def sq x:Integer => [mul x x] end def gt2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Boolean][a gt b]] end def bigger (FnUtil.on gt2/v sq/v) end (bigger 3 5)
import "boru:fn-util"  def sq x:Integer => [mul x x] end def gt2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Boolean][a gt b]] end def bigger (FnUtil.on gt2/v sq/v) end (bigger 5 3)
import "boru:fn-util"  def f fn x:Integer Integer [add 1 x] end def m (FnUtil.memoize f/v) end (m 4)
# The wrapper applied as a VALUE — the two-survivor paren re-steps it —
# dispatches on its own signature: `const` here is the wrapper, never the
# registered singleton-type maker (the compiled lane answered 99 before the
# thirty-fifth increment).
import "boru:fn-util"  ((FnUtil.const 7) 99)
column3: an applied const wrapper is the wrapper, not the `const` word

column1: # The read consumes its arity inside its own statement; what follows the
# `;` is the next statement's.
import "boru:fn-util"  def k (FnUtil.const 7) end k 1 ; 3
column3: the bare read applies over its statement's window

column1: # A 0-param wrapper applies on its bare read.
import "boru:fn-util"  def f x:Integer => [add 1 x] end def p (FnUtil.partial f/v 10) end (p)
column3: partial over a unary fn: the wrapper takes no argument

column1: # The curried chain (graduated 2026-09-08, the thirty-sixth increment): the
# claim carries the RESULT's shape, every level a unary wrapper returning the
# next, so each def-bound level models its own dispatch.
import "boru:fn-util"  def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]] end def c (FnUtil.curry sub2/v) end def c10 (c 10) end (c10 3)
column3: curry: one argument at a time

column1: import "boru:fn-util"  def sub3 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer c:Integer][Integer][a sub (b sub c)]] end def c (FnUtil.curry sub3/v) end def c1 (c 10) end def c2 (c1 3) end (c2 1)
# GRADUATED 2026-09-10 (the forty-ninth increment), from
# lang/spec/frontier/frontier-fn-util.tsv. A NAMED fn value reached as a call
# whose match failed used to refuse the WHOLE program: the site's note read
# "there is no call here to compile", which is true and beside the point — a
# mirror needs something that RAISES IDENTICALLY, not a call, and on the
# uncaught top line over operands the runtime match examines unchanged, a
# terminal OpTrap is exactly that. Both rows now compile to that trap and
# raise the interpreter's own error, caret and `/v` hint included.
import "boru:fn-util"  FnUtil.flip 5
column3: flip refuses a non-function operand at dispatch

column3: curry refuses a non-function operand at dispatch
